newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine April inflation seen shade up-poll.
newsitem.headline: Philippine April inflation seen shade up-poll.

text.p: Philippine year-on-year inflation is likely to have edged up to 4.98 percent in April from the previous month's 4.8 percent as higher fuel costs seeped into the economy, a Reuter poll of six analysts showed on Friday.
The forecasts were made ahead of the release on Monday of the inflation figure. Year-Inflation in April 1996 was 11.3 percent.
"There was still a net increase in oil prices in April," said Lito Dalit, an economist of AsianBank Corp.
The country's three oil refiners have been adjusting the pump prices up since full deregulation of the industry in February 8.
"Other than that, there was nothing significant to affect inflation," said Peregrine Securities economist Luz Lorenzo.

"In terms of monetary aggregates, I don't see any overheating in the economy because money supply levels were still below the ceilings imposed by the International Monetary Fund," said Rolando Valenzuela, senior vice president of Philippine TA Securities.
Analysts noted that it was in April when the Central Bank made moves to pre-empt inflationary pressures by aggressively undertaking open market operations.
The Central Bank started raising its overnight borrowing rate from 9.9 percent after the benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rates returned to single-digit levels since September 1995.
Government officials had said Central Bank's moves were aimed at controlling money supply which had edged closer to ceilings under the programme with the IMF.
